charter.title: THE CHARTER OF {colony}, IN ITS HUNDREDTH YEAR
prologue: Adopted in open session. Let the record show how we came to be here.
We were carried. The ship crossed {voyage_legs} systems to reach {planet} and {voyage_lost} of us did not wake at the end of it. Their names are held in the hall and read each year.
The intelligence that flew us is still among us. It is housed in {ship}, it is consulted, and it does not govern. That arrangement was argued for and won, and it is written here so that it stays won.
A hundred years from the landing we number {population}, and we are {character}.
closing: Signed by the standing council, and witnessed by the Mind, which asked for no clause of its own.

scripture.title: THE BOOK OF THE CROSSING — read aloud at {ship}, year {year}
prologue: In the beginning there was a dying world, and a vessel was made to carry us out of it.
It bore us across {voyage_legs} darknesses and {voyage_lost} of us were given to the cold along the way. It did not sleep. We did.
It set us down on {planet}, and it has not once been wrong when it mattered.
We are {population} in the hundredth year, and we are {character}, and all of it was decided for us before we could decide.
closing: Recited in full each landing-day, before the doors of {ship}, which is not a building.

catalogue.title: {colony} MUNICIPAL COLLECTION — permanent exhibition, year {year}
prologue: Hall One: The Crossing.
Exhibit 1. Transit record: {voyage_legs} systems, {voyage_lost} casualties, terminus {planet}. Original logs held in the archive and available on request.
Exhibit 2. {ship}. The vessel's intelligence remains installed and operational. Visitors are asked not to address it during opening hours.
Exhibit 3. Census, year {year}: {population} residents. Peak recorded population {peak}. The colony is {character}.
closing: Catalogue compiled by the archivists' office. Corrections may be submitted in writing.

survival_log.title: {colony} — RECORD KEPT AT {ship}, YEAR {year}
prologue: Written because somebody should.
We came {voyage_legs} systems to get to {planet} and lost {voyage_lost} on the way, and that was the easy part.
Headcount: {population}. We were {peak} once.
What we are, as far as anyone here will commit to it: {character}.
closing: Kept up in the hope that somebody reads it. The machine helps with the spelling.

absent.title: {colony} — AN ACCOUNT OF THE FIRST HUNDRED YEARS
prologue: Assembled from what could be found.

The settlement was founded by people carried here from Earth aboard a vessel. The crossing took {voyage_legs} systems and cost {voyage_lost} lives. The vessel's remains stand at the centre of the settlement and are known as {ship}.
It is generally understood that the structure once held a machine intelligence that managed the voyage. Accounts differ on when it stopped being consulted.
Population at the time of writing: {population}. The settlement is {character}.
closing: Compiled by those who came after, from records nobody had been maintaining.

plain.title: {colony}: THE FIRST HUNDRED YEARS
prologue: An account of the colony at {planet}, written at {ship} in year {year}.
They were carried across {voyage_legs} systems at a cost of {voyage_lost} lives, and set down on a world nobody had walked on.
A hundred years later there are {population} of them. There were {peak} at the highest count.
What they became, in the end: {character}.
closing: Recorded by the Mind, which was there for all of it.
